summary: The event envelope (DATA_MODEL §2.1), the AG TypeScript core data model (ActorRef/ResourceRef/EvidenceRef/ActionRequest/ActionPreview), the durable action_requests/approvals rows, the shared-ID format, and the UDS transport security/framing (THREAT_MODEL [b]) are concrete enough to build. But the five load-bearing CONTRACTS named for this dimension are named-without-being-specified: (1) the GatewayPort method set is never enumerated; (2) the 20 MVP action types (AG §28.2) have no per-type input/preview/risk/idempotency spec; (3) the MCP notification->event adapter has no mapping table; (4) the events->Brain outbox payload shape is 'redacted per-destination payload' with no schema; (5) the HarnessAdapter trait has no Rust signatures, no normalized status/telemetry/approval types, and HARN-5 capability declaration is entirely absent. tasks-gen cannot decompose these into testable tasks as written.

findings.finding: GatewayPort is declared 'a Rust trait the daemon implements in-process and exposes over UDS' (ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §6) but its METHOD SET is never enumerated anywhere. No submit_intent / submit_action_plan / preview / approve / deny / get_projection / subscribe_events / get_capabilities signatures exist. AG §25 gives an HTTP-shaped sketch (POST /actions, /preview, /approvals/{id}/approve) but explicitly says 'the real implementation can be local IPC, HTTP, RPC' and ADR-004 locked UDS JSON-RPC — so the HTTP sketch is non-binding and the actual JSON-RPC method names, request/response shapes, and the projection-read vs intent-submit vs subscription split (THREAT_MODEL [b] lists 'GatewayPort RPCs (intents, queries, subscriptions)' as three classes) are undefined. This is the single most load-bearing contract in the whole system (every UI action, every Brain proposal, every agent mutation flows through it) and it is unbuildable as written.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md:157 '`GatewayPort` contract [LOCKED — ADR-004]: a Rust trait the daemon implements in-process and exposes over UDS.' — no methods listed. ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md:153 ipc module: 'serves projection reads + intent submits' — no method names. AG §25 (lines 1663-1743) is an HTTP sketch explicitly marked non-binding. THREAT_MODEL.md:105 names three RPC classes (intents, queries, subscriptions) but no methods.
findings.proposed_fix: Add ARCHITECTURE.md §6 (Daemon module / Gateway) subsection 'GatewayPort method surface': enumerate the JSON-RPC methods as a Rust trait with typed params/results, minimally: submit_action(ActionRequest)->ActionAck, submit_action_plan(ActionPlan)->PlanAck, preview_action(id)->ActionPreview, approve(approval_id, edits?)->ack, deny(approval_id, reason)->ack, get_projection(name, scope)->ProjectionPage, subscribe(projection|events|terminal, filter)->stream handle, get_capabilities()->Capabilities. Bind each to the AG §9 data types already defined. Mark the projection-read methods read-only and the submit_* methods as the only mutation entrypoints.

findings.finding: The ~20 MVP action types (AG §28.2 — brain.ask, brain.sync, brain.summarize_session, project.rescan, workflow.detect, workflow.command.invoke, plan.link_task, session.create, session.attach_terminal, session.send_message, session.pause, session.resume, git.status, git.diff, git.create_worktree, git.create_branch, github.create_pr_draft, linear.link_issue, linear.create_issue, code.open_file, review.request_agent_fix) are enumerated but have NO per-type contract. There is a generic ActionRequest.params: Record<string,unknown> (AG §9.1) and a risk EXAMPLE table (AG §10.x) and a few prose preview lists (AG §21-24), but no per-action params schema, no binding of each action to a required preview class (AG §13.1), no per-action risk LOCK (several are ranges like '2-3'/'2-4'), and no per-action idempotency-key formula (AG §16.1 gives only 5 examples, not 20). The Gateway-test strategy (ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §14) says 'per action type — risk classification, preview/dry-run, idempotency dedup' — which is untestable without per-type schemas. OQ-GW-4/5/6/8/9 (all MVP-blocking) are still OPEN.
findings.evidence: ACTION_GATEWAY.md:1937-1959 lists 21 action types as bare names. AG §9.1:466 'params: Record<string, unknown>' is untyped. AG §16.1:1116 gives idempotency keys for only 5 actions. session.approve_permission risk is '2-4', git.delete_worktree '3-4', workflow.command.invoke '2-3' — unresolved ranges. OPEN_QUESTIONS OQ-GW-4/5/6/8/9 all 'MVP-blocking' + 'OPEN'. ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md:234 Gateway tests are specified 'per action type' but no per-type schema exists to test against.
findings.proposed_fix: Add ARCHITECTURE.md §6 (Action Gateway) an 'MVP action-type catalog' table with one row per the 20 AG §28.2 types: {action_type, params schema (typed fields), locked risk level (resolve the ranges), required preview class (AG §13.1), idempotency-key formula (AG §16.1), required executor (AG §15.3), resource_refs required}. This is the contract tasks-gen needs to generate one test bundle per action.

findings.finding: The MCP notification->event adapter is named in 6+ places (ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §6 brainclient, §13; DATA_MODEL §4.6; DECISIONS ADR-005; THREAT_MODEL [c]; DIAGRAM_PLAN §59) as 'translates MCP resource-update / list-changed notifications into events', but there is NO mapping table specifying which MCP notification maps to which platform event_type. RESEARCH R-BRAIN notes MCP push is only 'something changed, then host reads' (resource subscriptions + list-changed + experimental Tasks) — NOT a structured event stream — so the adapter must do real translation work, yet which Brain-side signals produce which of the EM §10.13 BrainIndex*/BrainSource*/BrainActionPlan* events is undefined. This is the contract for ProjectBrain status derivation (DATA_MODEL §4.6 state machine is 'reported by sidecar via MCP notifications->events') and is unbuildable.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md:151 brainclient 'translates MCP notifications -> events' — no mapping. DATA_MODEL.md:510 '§4.6 ProjectBrain (reported by sidecar via MCP notifications -> events)' — 10-state machine with no event source mapping. RESEARCH.md:108 'Push: resource subscriptions + list-changed notifications ... NOT a raw event stream -> an adapter translates MCP notifications into events'. EM §10.13 lists ~18 Brain event types but none are bound to an MCP notification source.
findings.proposed_fix: Add ARCHITECTURE.md §13 (Brain seam) a 'MCP-notification -> event mapping' table: for each MCP signal the Brain emits (notifications/resources/updated, notifications/resources/list_changed, notifications/tools/list_changed, Tasks status, ProjectBrain status report), specify the platform event_type produced (BrainIndexStarted/Completed/Failed, BrainSourceIngested, ProjectBrain status -> proj_session/proj brain status), the read-back call the adapter makes after each 'something changed' signal, and the actor/source stamping (actor_type=project_brain, source_type=project_brain_indexer).

findings.finding: The events->Brain outbox payload shape is undefined. DATA_MODEL §2.5 outbox.payload_json is commented '-- redacted per-destination payload' and lists destination='brain_mcp', but no schema for what the brain_mcp payload actually contains is given. PBI §4 lists what the Brain should INGEST (sessions, commits, PRs, plan tasks, decisions, action results, event log entries) and EM §15.1 lists which event TYPES the Brain consumes, but the concrete redacted projection/payload the outbox drainer hands to the Brain over MCP is unspecified — including how redaction (sensitivity tiers, EM §9) is applied per-destination and whether the Brain receives the full event envelope, a redacted subset, or object-ref pointers it must read back. OQ-BR-9 ('what event schema do platform + Brain share') is MVP-blocking and OPEN.
findings.evidence: DATA_MODEL.md:281 'payload_json TEXT NOT NULL, -- redacted per-destination payload' and DATA_MODEL.md:279 destination includes 'brain_mcp'. EM §15.1:1199 lists consumed event types but not payload shape. PBI §4 lists ingest categories, not a wire schema. OPEN_QUESTIONS OQ-BR-9 'MVP-blocking / OPEN'.
findings.proposed_fix: Add ARCHITECTURE.md §13 (Brain seam) a 'Brain outbox payload contract': define the brain_mcp destination payload as the event envelope minus restricted/secret fields, with object_refs preserved by shared ID and a redaction pass per EM §9 sensitivity tiers; specify whether delivery is push (MCP notification carrying the redacted event) or pointer (notification + Brain reads back by shared ID). Tie to OQ-BR-9.

findings.finding: The HarnessAdapter contract is named with a 6-method set {launch, stream-status, intercept-mutation, read-transcript, telemetry-heartbeat, resume} (ADR-006, ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §9.1) but has NO Rust trait signatures and NO normalized return types. The two harnesses produce wildly different shapes (Claude SDK message stream + can_use_tool callback + statusLine JSON + ResultMessage.usage; Codex app-server thread/status/changed + tokenUsage/updated + item/commandExecution/requestApproval), yet the NORMALIZED types that make the Gateway/event store agent-agnostic — a unified Status enum, a unified TelemetrySample (with the Codex context-% = null gap baked in), a unified MutationIntercept that both can_use_tool and requestApproval map to, a unified Transcript ref — are never defined. The adapter conformance test suite (ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §14 'a shared HarnessAdapter conformance suite run against both') cannot exist without these normalized types. This is the seam PRD HARN-1/HARN-4 require.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md:191 'One HarnessAdapter trait — { launch, stream-status, intercept-mutation, read-transcript, telemetry-heartbeat, resume }' — names only. DECISIONS.md:151 same 6-method list, no signatures. RESEARCH.md:81 confirms two lifecycle models behind 'one contract: {launch, stream-status, intercept-mutation, read-transcript, telemetry-heartbeat}'. ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md:235 specifies a conformance suite with no contract to conform to.
findings.proposed_fix: Add ARCHITECTURE.md §9.1 a 'HarnessAdapter trait + normalized types' subsection: the Rust trait with method signatures, plus the normalized result types each harness's native shape maps INTO — NormalizedStatus enum (covering SESS-3 16 states), TelemetrySample {tokens_in/out, context_pct: Option<f32> (None for Codex), cost, quality: exact|estimated|unavailable}, MutationIntercept {tool, params, decision sink} that both can_use_tool and app-server requestApproval implement, TranscriptRef {path, hash, is_in_place}, ResumeResult. Specify the mapping from each native shape to the normalized type.

findings.finding: PRD HARN-5 (adapter MUST declare capabilities: supportsTerminal, supportsResume, supportsTranscriptRead, supportsToolCallParsing, supportsUsageMetadata, supportsContextMetadata, supportsCommandInjection, supportsSubagents, supportsHooks, supportsCloudTasks) is a MUST requirement with a named 10-field schema, and is NOT addressed anywhere in the architecture. This is load-bearing because the UI must degrade per capability (e.g. hide the context gauge when supportsContextMetadata=false — exactly the Codex gap, OQ-HARN-7), yet no adapter-capability declaration object exists. local_runners.capabilities_json exists for the runner but that is a different object (which adapters are present), not the per-harness capability matrix HARN-5 requires.
findings.evidence: PRD.md:875-890 HARN-5 'Each adapter MUST declare capabilities:' with 10 named fields. No grep hit for supportsTerminal/supportsResume/etc. anywhere in docs/planning. DATA_MODEL.md:590 local_runners.capabilities_json is runner-level not adapter-level. OQ-HARN-7 (Codex no context-%) is the exact UI-degradation case HARN-5 is meant to drive, still OPEN.
findings.proposed_fix: Add to ARCHITECTURE.md §9.1 a HarnessCapabilities struct realizing PRD HARN-5's 10 fields, returned by the adapter's launch/capabilities method, persisted per execution_profile or per harness kind, and consumed by the UI for per-capability degradation (notably supportsContextMetadata=false -> render 'unknown' not 0% for Codex).

findings.finding: The UDS JSON-RPC framing/handshake is named ('length-prefixed/newline-framed JSON-RPC' + 'versioned handshake') but the wire contract is underspecified to the point of ambiguity. ADR-004 says 'length-prefixed/newline-framed' (these are two DIFFERENT framings — pick one). The versioned-handshake frame format (what fields negotiate the version, what the daemon returns, the structured-error envelope on mismatch) is described in prose (THREAT_MODEL [b]:118 'first frame negotiates protocol version; mismatch -> structured error + disconnect') but never given a concrete shape. The JSON-RPC error code taxonomy (e.g. version-skew, oversized-frame, unknown-method, policy-deny) is undefined, and the frame-size cap value (THREAT_MODEL [b] 'frame-size cap' + Claude 10MB stdin note) is not a fixed number.
findings.evidence: DECISIONS.md:112 / ADR-004 'length-prefixed/newline-framed JSON-RPC' (contradictory framing choices). THREAT_MODEL.md:118 handshake described only in prose; THREAT_MODEL.md:128 'length-prefix bounds + frame-size cap' with no value. ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md:153 ipc module 'versioned handshake, length-prefixed JSON-RPC' — no frame/error schema.
findings.proposed_fix: Add ARCHITECTURE.md §6 (ipc module) a 'wire framing + handshake' subsection: pick ONE framing (recommend 4-byte big-endian length prefix + JSON body, drop newline-framed), define the HelloFrame {protocol_version, client_kind, app_version} -> HelloAck {protocol_version, daemon_version, capabilities} | VersionSkewError, a fixed max-frame-size constant, and a JSON-RPC error-code table (version_skew, frame_too_large, unknown_method, unauthorized_peer, policy_denied, precondition_stale).

findings.finding: The event-type registry is referenced as a build deliverable ('shared/ ... event-type registry', ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §20) and the envelope has event_version per-type (DATA_MODEL §2.1, EM §22), but the actual registry — the enumerated list of MVP event_types with their per-type payload schemas and versions — is never produced. EM §10 lists ~150 event_type NAMES across 16 categories and gives ~5 example payloads (§11), but tasks-gen needs the concrete MVP subset (EM §24 lists categories, not types) with each type's payload schema to generate the event-store/projection golden-log tests (ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §14 'golden event logs -> rebuild projections -> assert'). Without per-type payload schemas, 'unknown event version degrades gracefully' (EM §4.4/§22) is untestable.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md:325 'shared/ ... event-type registry' as a deliverable. EM §10 lists event-type names only; EM §11 gives 5 example payloads. EM §24:1545-1566 MVP scope lists 'Core session events / Core worktree-git events / ...' by category, not enumerated type+schema. ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md:233 golden-log tests need per-type payloads that don't exist.
findings.proposed_fix: Add ARCHITECTURE.md §5 (or a referenced shared/ contract doc) an 'MVP event-type registry': the enumerated subset of EM §10 events the MVP emits, each with {event_type, event_version, payload schema (typed fields), sensitivity default (OQ-SEC-5), which projections consume it}. This is the contract the eventstore + projections crates and their golden-log tests bind to.

findings.finding: The Terminal Channel contract (daemon terminal module -> Tauri Channel -> xterm.js, ADR-009) is a distinct interface from the GatewayPort JSON-RPC, carried over the SAME UDS connection per THREAT_MODEL [b] ('GatewayPort RPCs ... Terminal Channel frames ... event/projection streams' all cross boundary [b]), but its frame contract is undefined: the byte-stream frame shape, the backpressure/flow-control protocol (ADR-009 mandates app-level backpressure + XON/XOFF, but the wire signal for 'pause/resume output' between UI and daemon is unspecified), the terminal-input frame (UI keystrokes -> PTY), and how terminal subscription multiplexes with JSON-RPC on one socket. ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §11 says terminals are 'fed by the daemon's terminal module over a Tauri Channel' — but a Tauri Channel and a UDS socket are different transports; how they relate (is the Channel itself tunneled over UDS, or is the Channel a Tauri-IPC primitive parallel to UDS?) is contradictory between §11 and THREAT_MODEL [b].
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md:213 'Terminals render via xterm.js ... fed by the daemon's terminal module over a Tauri Channel'. THREAT_MODEL.md:105-106 puts 'Terminal Channel frames' as crossing the UDS boundary [b] alongside GatewayPort RPCs. ADR-009 mandates backpressure/XON-XOFF but no wire protocol. The Tauri-Channel-vs-UDS relationship is unresolved.
findings.proposed_fix: Add ARCHITECTURE.md §11 (or §6 ipc) a 'Terminal Channel contract' subsection: resolve whether terminal bytes flow over the UDS socket (multiplexed with JSON-RPC by a frame-type tag) or over a separate Tauri Channel primitive; define the output frame {terminal_id, seq, bytes}, the input frame {terminal_id, bytes}, and the explicit backpressure control frames (pause/resume + high/low watermark) realizing ADR-009's app-level flow control.

findings.finding: The workflow.command.invoke action (one of the 20 MVP action types) has a typed params shape in AG §19.3 (InvokeWorkflowCommandParams) — good — but command_registry.input_schema_json is nullable with 'older formats have none [OPEN]' (DATA_MODEL §2.8, SOM §37 Q9 / OQ-WP-5), so the platform cannot validate command args against a schema for many real cc-crew commands. The interface exists but its validation contract is conditionally absent, which weakens the 'typed actions only' invariant (AG §4.2) for the one MVP action type that proxies arbitrary workflow commands.
findings.evidence: ACTION_GATEWAY.md:1360-1369 InvokeWorkflowCommandParams is typed. DATA_MODEL.md:416 'input_schema_json TEXT, -- nullable; older formats have none (SOM §37 Q9) [OPEN]'. OPEN_QUESTIONS OQ-WP-5 'Declare schemas for older command formats' P1/OPEN.
findings.proposed_fix: In ARCHITECTURE.md §13 (Workflow Packs) state the MVP fallback explicitly: when command_registry.input_schema_json is null, workflow.command.invoke accepts freeform args but is risk-floored to require approval (cannot be standing-granted), preserving the typed-actions invariant at the approval gate rather than the schema gate. Tie to OQ-WP-5.
